title: Favourite musicians: Lewis and Dodds on ensemble playing
summary: He listens only to jazz, prefers ensemble to solos, and names George Lewis and Johnny Dodds, especially with King Oliver.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: I wondered about who some of your favorite musicians were, just in general, any instrument or any approach to jazz. Not necessarily jazz, that's what you like.

Well, it's jazz. I listen to jazz, I suppose, only. It just doesn't seem to be time to listen to jazz enough, much less to other things. I can't, I'm not, not sort of, madly interested in solo work as such, so that I listen more for ensemble and try and play that in the band. And, undoubtedly, Lewis must feature strongly in it. Although I see quite a lot of fault in his playing and all this sort of thing. He's got the great sort of commanding glory that he plays hot. That's the thing that counts. Dodds, I still very much enjoy listening to Dodds all the time, even though I don't attempt to play that much in his style. Although, the Dodds that played with King Oliver is a fine style, which I probably do try to play a bit like, because that's just about a perfect New Orleans ensemble style, I think. Well, then there's, I'm assuming, with the Jelly Roll, Morton, and things. I like jazz, you know, generally. It's hard to.
